summary: The PCs' post: the Wasp Marshals for the southeast, overseeing all Wasp bounty hunting in six domains (Fox, Sparrow, Kakita, Etsuko, Reiji, Daika) and reporting to Tsuruchi Kyoma a few times a week. They guide the Inspectors, may investigate personally, and receive official guests. The PCs are of the upper 7th rank, the Inspectors of the lower 7th. They replaced Tsuruchi Kaminari, Tsuruchi Danji and Tsuruchi Okihito, promoted in 1130 to be Marshals in the Yasuki Estates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: The Wasp officer assigned to each of the six domains under the Marshals (the PCs), one per domain, of the lower 7th rank, each with a small team of Escorts. Not to be confused with a tariff inspector at a city gate.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: Members of an Inspector's small team who help collect bounties and deliver the fugitive (or head) to wherever the bounty was placed to claim the reward. Tsuruchi Hideki is an Escort.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: The chain of command for Wasp bounty hunting in the southeast: Tsuruchi Kyoma, then the PCs as Marshals (haribugyo), then one Inspector (metsuke) per domain, then each Inspector's Escorts (gosonin). The campaign wiki page has the org chart.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

term: Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies
summary: Tsuruchi Kyoma's title: the Wasp envoy overseeing bounty operations among the Wasp's southern allies (the Three Man Alliance). He keeps residences in Shinden Kitsune and Shiro Suzume; the PCs run his office while household stewards run his homes.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Byakuya

summary: The PCs' boss: Distinguished Plenipotentiary to the Southern Allies of the Wasp, a close friend of the Wasp daimyo Tsuruchi, overseeing bounty work among the southern allies while focusing on cementing the Three Man Alliance through long nights of shared cups. Born Kyo Kyoma of the Kyo house; at the 1110 banquet he killed Kyo Fumikazu, who was about to stab Tsuruchi in the back. Husband of Tsuruchi Hitomi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the northernmost Daidoji domain of the Crane Clan; capital Shiro Etsuko. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Nobumasa. Imperial magistrate: Otomo Genzo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the northeasternmost Hida domain of the Crab Clan; capital Shiro Reiji. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Fumitake. Imperial magistrate: Seppun Sena.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: One of the six domains the PCs oversee as Marshals: the Bayushi domain of the Scorpion Clan west of the Kitsune forest; capital Shiro Daika. Wasp Inspector: Tsuruchi Fumikazu. Imperial magistrate: Hantei Kairi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Wasp hierarchy

summary: A tiny minor clan founded about 15 years before the campaign by Tsuruchi, first of his name, with Crane backing; its holdings are the single mountain province of Hachinaga. Its charter lets every Wasp samurai act as an Imperial magistrate to pursue Imperial bounties, which are a large share of its income. Its three lineages are the Tsuruchi, Ami and Kyoma lineages, and its chancellery is "the Crane wives". It leads the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Emperor's charter creating the Wasp Clan (1116). It grants every Wasp samurai the authority to act as an Imperial magistrate for the purpose of pursuing Imperial bounties, so every Wasp is a potential bounty hunter.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's legacy

summary: Tsuruchi, first of his name: founder and daimyo of the Wasp Clan, born Bayushi no Kyo Tsuruchi of the Shin lineage. After his parents were killed at a banquet in 1110 and the Lion took Hachinaga Keep, he became a ronin Imperial bounty hunter famed for his bow ("A single arrow, a single life"), retook the keep in 1115, executed his treacherous uncle Matsu no Zenji Ginjiro with the broken sword Isshin, and was made daimyo of the new clan in 1116. He carries no sword at home and declared there shall be no Ancestral Sword of the Wasp. Married to Tsuruchi Naomi; their son is Ichiro.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

term: A single arrow, a single life
summary: Tsuruchi's motto as a bounty hunter, who preferred to strike down fugitives with his bow rather than challenge them to duels.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's career as an Imperial bounty hunter

summary: The mountainous province that is the whole of the Wasp Clan's holdings, guarding the narrow Hachinaga pass through the Spine of the World Mountains about 150 miles inland. Ruled by the Shin lineage for over a thousand years, first under the Scorpion (Kyo house).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Wasp Clan's seat. The broken blade of the sword Isshin is still embedded in the floor of its great hall, and Wasp samurai (and many guests) rarely carry swords inside it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's legacy

summary: The ancestral sword of the Shin lineage. Tsuruchi surrendered it to his uncle Ginjiro in 1111, took it back in 1115 and snapped it in the floor of Hachinaga Keep's great hall, executing Ginjiro with the broken shard. The blade stays in the floor; the hilt is on an ancestral shrine in the same room.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's revenge

summary: The lineage descended from Bayushi Shin that ruled Hachinaga province for a thousand years as part of the Scorpion's Kyo house; Tsuruchi's birth lineage and the core of the Wasp's Tsuruchi lineage.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: A vassal house of the Bayushi Family (Scorpion Clan), daimyo Bayushi no Kyo Haruka. Tsuruchi and Tsuruchi Kyoma were both originally of the Kyo; the Shin lineage once served it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: A vassal house of the Matsu Family (Lion Clan) bordering Wasp lands to the north; daimyo Matsu no Zenji Kana. Tsuruchi's mother Natsu was a Zenji, and the Zenji took Hachinaga Keep in 1111.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign

summary: The Wasp lineage made up mostly of the original Shin lineage plus other former Scorpion who joined the Wasp; headed on the chancellery by Tsuruchi Naomi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives

summary: The Wasp's "peasantborn" lineage: mostly the peasant yoriki who helped Tsuruchi as a bounty hunter and the mercenaries who retook Hachinaga Keep, raised to the samurai caste. Headed by Tsuruchi Ami, wife of Tsuruchi Takuan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > The wives

summary: The Wasp lineage joined by nearly all the samurai from other clans (and many ronin) who came to the Wasp after its founding; the least cohesive of the three. Headed by Tsuruchi Hitomi, Tsuruchi Kyoma's wife.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > The wives

summary: The Wasp Clan chancellery: three Crane courtiers given as wives to Tsuruchi and his two most loyal retainers - Tsuruchi Naomi (Tsuruchi lineage), Tsuruchi Ami (Ami lineage) and Tsuruchi Hitomi (Kyoma lineage). The name alludes to the fable of the crane wife.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives

summary: Tsuruchi's wife, youngest daughter of the Crane Champion Doji Kuwanen, one of the Crane wives and head of the Tsuruchi lineage. In 1130 she began matchmaking for their 12-year-old son Ichiro.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Naomi

summary: Chancellor of the Ami ("peasantborn") lineage, one of the Crane wives, born Doji no Tsume Ami; wife of Tsuruchi Takuan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Ami

summary: Tsuruchi Kyoma's wife, one of the Crane wives and head of the Kyoma lineage; born a Kakita. Her brother Kakita Daini died losing the ink-flight (Akechi) scrolls to Matsu Agetoki in a wager, and she took the name Hitomi pledging to reclaim them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Hitomi

summary: Silk hangings of calligraphy painted with ink-dipped arrows by the archer-poet Kakita Akechi. Lost by Kakita Daini to Matsu no Masao Agetoki in an archery wager twenty years ago.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Hitomi

summary: Wasp Minister of Retainers, Tsuruchi's most accomplished peasant informant from his bounty hunting days and the only peasantborn Wasp to merit a Crane wife (Tsuruchi Ami).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Ami

summary: The 12-year-old eldest son of Tsuruchi and Tsuruchi Naomi, heir to the Wasp, who plans to take the name Tsuruchi Ichiro at his gempukku.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Crane Wives > Tsuruchi Naomi

summary: Household steward running Tsuruchi Kyoma's residence in Sparrow lands (Shiro Suzume), an old friend of Kyoma's from the Kyo house, raising his young daughter Hatsuko.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Byakuya

summary: Steward of Tsuruchi Kyoma's Fox Clan residence; deeply superstitious and a generous patron to the PCs, who gave them charms against fox mischief and amulets for entering the Kitsune Mori.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small red silk pouch bearing the seal of the Kitsune household sponsoring a journey; carried openly, the wood's fox-spirits leave the bearer alone.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small brass bell on a staff or pack; while it rings on the path, fox-illusions cannot easily replace the way back.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small black iron pin worn against the skin, which disrupts low-grade fox glamours.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: An amulet Tsuruchi Tatsuki gave the PCs for the Kitsune Mori: a small disc of obsidian or smoky quartz worn at the neck that reveals whether a path, hut or face is real.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Wasp Clan NPCs > Tsuruchi Tatsuki

summary: The pact of the three minor clans of the southeast - the Wasp (at its head), the Fox and the Sparrow - formed in 1117: a military defense pact and a voting caucus on the Imperial chancellery, where all three vote together. All three owe favors to the Crane.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Three Man Alliance

summary: Minor clan whose lands ring the Kitsune Mori, descended from ancient shamans and the shapechanging black fox Osusuki; the Kitsune Family. Rich from the forest (lumber, charcoal, white charcoal, incense), with five lineages (the ruling Kitsune plus Toke, Hokke, Saike and Nanke for the four cardinal provinces). Daimyo: Kitsune Ryosei. Wasp ally in the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan

summary: The fox forest, third largest in the Empire, bordered by the Lion (north), Scorpion (west), Crane (east) and Crab (south); full of spirits and fox-spirits. The Fox Clan holds it, free of Imperial taxation; it watches outsiders who linger, especially on the Imperial road through Minami province.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan > The Kitsune Forest

summary: Fox Clan "shrine-grade" charcoal made from sacred oak, prized for its odorless, almost smokeless burn in shrines and tea ceremonies; overseen by the Fox Ministry of Rites and counterfeited by the bounty target "Kitsune Denhei".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan > The Fox Clan's economy

summary: Minor clan founded by the Crane noble Suzume (the Suzume Family) in the poor Sparrow Hills, where tenant farming is outlawed and Sparrow samurai live in the villages as village overseers sworn to poverty before Daikoku. Poor in rice and coin, they grow tea, mulberry and soybeans. Daimyo: Suzume Mukashino. Wasp ally in the Three Man Alliance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Sparrow Clan

summary: A Sparrow samurai posted to live in a farming village and manage it in place of a peasant headsman, sworn to a vow of poverty to Daikoku. Found nowhere else in the Empire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Sparrow Clan > Sparrow land management

summary: A Mantis (Shione family) sugarcane syndicate, said to be founded by smugglers and pirates, with armed outfits throughout this quarter of the Empire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: The war between the Lion and Crane clans that began in 1122 over Toshi Ranbo; the Three Man Alliance gave the Crane safe passage through Sparrow lands (not Hachinaga pass), and Wasp and Fox samurai helped defend the Sparrow hills.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Three Man Alliance > The Lion/Crane War

summary: A reward registered with an Imperial magistrate for bringing in a fugitive (or a summoned witness); the target is delivered to the magistrate who registered it, who pays out. Traditionally the collector keeps half, their superior takes a tenth, and the rest goes to the daimyo's treasury. Governed by the Doctrine of Three Steps. The campaign wiki explains how bounties work; the Imperial bulletin lists the open ones.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties

summary: The list of outstanding Imperial bounties distributed to local authorities; the campaign wiki keeps the current list (updated as the campaign goes).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: the small gift given to an Imperial magistrate when registering a bounty.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift with no expectation of value, given instead of a token gift when the petitioner already knows the magistrate.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: the payment made to the magistrate when a bounty is accepted (a tithe of the bounty), or a gift that funds the bounty itself.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift to a local Imperial magistrate who pays out a bounty on someone else's behalf, when the hunter has no prior relationship with them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

summary: One of the formal gifts around bounties: a gift recognizing the trouble a request puts a magistrate to, such as forcing an awkward summons.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Registering a bounty

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): an old hermit with long gray hair and a goiter on the right of his neck, who struck Bayushi no Daika Koharu from behind with an axe in the Kitsune forest, accusing him of hunting foxes; travels with disciples.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): an unnamed Yasuki smuggler who sails with forged papers and kimono of many clans, his men fighting in the Crab style.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (100 koku): six to eight bandits robbing barges at the oxbow west of Kyuden Kakita, fleeing into Zenji marshes; some carry Crab-style tetsubo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (75 koku): the bandit lord who robbed the manor of Kakita Hikai, county magistrate of Seitoyama, and should bear a scar from left ear to chin. "Kage" (shadow) is a common bandit alias.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (75 koku): supplied obsidian to the traitor Shinjo Jotsu; scarred stomach and chest, always carries obsidian; seen in Shinden Kitsune.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty (75 koku) posted by the Fox for a branch cut from a sacred humming camphor tree in the Kitsune Forest before Setsubun, probably for a musical instrument; Kakita Ikura the musician left the festival suddenly.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): a Mantis man who fled Kyuden Kakita rather than answer Kakita Foruku's duel challenge; seen in Shiro Suzume.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): two men and a woman who robbed Daidoji no Etsuko Azami of silk; she splashed the men with indigo dye that stains their hands and nails.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): struck a steward and attacked the Witch Hunter Kuni Nakadai at the Sovereign Temple of Hotei in Kyuden Kakita; seen there in pilgrim's clothes.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): born Mirumoto Miyuki, exiled from Dragon lands for killing a Shosuro actress, then joined the Togashi Ise Zumi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (50 koku): eldest daughter of the Fox shugenja Kitsune Shunichi, who accepted Bayushi no Daika Isoshi's duel challenge and then left to "meditate"; the Fox daimyo will not compel her return. She is a PC in the Tuesday group and is not a Wasp.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (40 koku): bandits in the southern Sparrow foothills, raiding northern Daidoji lands; their leader stutters.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty (40 koku) to identify whoever sells counterfeit Kitsune white charcoal in Kakita and Etsuko lands under the name of "Kitsune Denhei", a Fox merchant who does not exist.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (30 koku): tall, thin bandits who rob travelers mid-ford in the Mugi-arai-gawa between Fox and Daidoji lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (25 koku): three men who robbed a Fox charcoal merchant south of Shinden Kitsune; one has maho-cult scars on his forearms.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): a former porter missing parts of two right-hand fingers who stole crates of lacquerware at the docks.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): wreckers moving channel markers near Uminari north of Shiro Etsuko; one has a broken nose.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (20 koku): wanted for questioning by the Masao domain; expected at Kyuden Kakita for the Doll Festival.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (15 koku): Scorpion charcoal merchant who never paid the Fox for a shipment of white charcoal.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (15 koku): Flying Spears bandit from Aoyagi in the Reiji domain; big, nearly 6 feet, leans left from a hip injury.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (10 koku): a very polite con artist posing as a dignitary's advance man to cheat innkeepers in Etsuko and Kakita lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (10 koku): an attacker of Kakita Aichiko whose right ear she partially severed.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Bounty target (5 koku): a rigged-dice cheat who escaped forced labor at Shiro Suzume; gap-toothed sleight-of-hand master.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: The lawful form of private vengeance: declared by those personally wronged against those who wronged them, it extends to every descendant of each named person's paternal great-grandfather on both sides, any of whom may lawfully kill any on the other side. Outsiders gain nothing from it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Blood Feuds

summary: A messy all-hands Wasp job: delivering an Imperial summons to Ikoma Yuan at a teahouse ended with the Ikoma shugenja Ikoma Tsai killed. His father Ikoma Wataemon and brothers Ikoma Naohira and Ikoma Ietsugu declared a blood feud on the Wasp present, which reaches the PCs through their relatives; the three are on their way south. The source of the Righteous Sting and Venomous Sting advantage and disadvantage.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Family Reckoning

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: Family Reckoning advantage: your relative at the teahouse acted honorably; your Rank counts higher, and the party's too.

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Family Reckoning disadvantage: your relative at the teahouse acted questionably; your Rank counts lower, and the party's too.

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: your household owes the Crane, who may ask you to advance their interests; refusing costs face.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: a letter of introduction from your lineage's chancellor; you count as higher Rank and Recognition with Wasp samurai.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Imperial officials see you as a troublemaker from past bounties.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: the Zenji house (and the Matsu) hate you for past bounty work on Lion samurai.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: a strong ally in the Sparrow, Fox or Mantis, with clan-specific favors.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom disadvantage: Scorpion contacts sometimes ask you to thwart a fellow Wasp's egregious behavior.

source.section: Custom advantages and disadvantages

summary: Wasp campaign custom advantage: seasoned bounty-hunting experience; free raises on etiquette, law, intimidation and underworld rolls about your authority.

summary: The rules of the Measure of Standing for what is appropriate between samurai of different ranks, including when one samurai is of "peer standing" with another (merits such as advantages shift perceived rank). Governs bounties, duels and arrests. The campaign wiki has the full explanation.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank

summary: The bears of the Kitsune Mori (tsukinowaguma, "moon-ring bear"), black with a pale crescent on the chest. The worst is the anamotazu, "the one with no den", a bear that never denned and hunts hungry through winter.

source.section: Bears of the Kitsune Mori

summary: The system of government ministries formalized by Hantei the Tenth, repeated at the Imperial, Clan, Family, House and provincial levels: Rites, Revenue, Retainers, War, Works and Justice. The chancellery sets policy; the ministries carry it out.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for shrines, temples, festivals and religious obligations, and the registers of births, marriages and deaths. The Imperial Minister of Rites is also the High Priestess of Amaterasu and decides which doctrines are heresy.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Rites

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for land taxes, business licenses and city-gate import tariffs. The Imperial Minister of Revenue is also called the Imperial Treasurer.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Revenue

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for samurai stipends, ranks, civil service exams and promotions. The Imperial ministry also awards honors and commendations.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Retainers

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for armies, weapons, armor, horses and maps. The Imperial Minister of War is the Shogun and oversees the Imperial legions.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of War

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for roads, walls, harbors, granaries and other public works, using corvee labor. At the Imperial level it also maintains the Kaiu Wall and the Imperial roads' waystations.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Works

summary: One of the Six Ministries, responsible for policing, bandit patrols, magistrates, courts and jails. The Imperial Minister of Justice is the Emerald Champion.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Ministry of Justice

summary: The council that sets policy, made up of chancellors who represent lineages (at the House level) or houses (at the Imperial level). The Imperial chancellery advises the Emperor and in practice decides most matters; the Three Man Alliance votes there as a bloc.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: Head of the Imperial chancellery, of the 14th rank; currently Kakita Yoshi, who backed the creation of the Wasp Clan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: The Imperial Chancellor, a Crane, who showed Tsuruchi his uncle's treacherous letter, promised Crane backing and arranged the Wasp Clan's charter.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Tsuruchi's revenge

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of War, who oversees the Imperial legions.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Revenue.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Justice, chosen by a dueling tournament to be the best duelist in the Empire and duel on the Emperor's behalf.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: The title of the Imperial Minister of Rites.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The Emperor's magistrate in each domain, under the Emerald Charter: handles disputes between samurai of different clans, Imperial tax collection and legion recruiting, and registers and pays out Imperial bounties. Has a large staff of Imperial yoriki. Each of the six domains the PCs oversee has one.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: An assistant to a magistrate (or official). The PCs are Tsuruchi Kyoma's yoriki; Tsuruchi began with former retainers as his yoriki.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Justice

summary: The 15 ranks of the samurai caste: 15 the Emperor; 14 the Imperial Chancellor and the Clan daimyo; 13 Family daimyo and Imperial Ministers; 12 House daimyo; 11 Chancellor; 10 Minister; 9 Deputy Minister; 8 Governor; 7 Provincial Minister; 6 Deputy Provincial Minister; 5 County Magistrate; 4 Squad Sergeant; 3 Corporal; 2 legionnaire; 1 unposted samurai. Each rank has an upper and lower level (7.5 is "the upper seventh rank").

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government

summary: The lord of a Clan, Family or House (ranks 14, 13 and 12).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A provincial governor (rank 8), who lives in the provincial city.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: Head of one of the six ministries at the provincial level (rank 7).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The official administering a county from its town (rank 5).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The peasant who oversees a village district from its main village.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The steward of a household or official's staff.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The servant who manages a samurai's household affairs.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: the largest grouping: the 7 Great Clans and the minor clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: each Great Clan has 3-5 Great Families, one of them ruling.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: a Family's ruling house or vassal house, each ruling one domain.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: a political coalition of samurai tracing to a notable ancestor; lineages with enough members sit on their house's chancellery.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: the land a House rules, about 70 miles across, usually about six provinces.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a domain overseen by a Governor from the provincial city; about six counties.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a province run by a County Magistrate from its town.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: A level of the hierarchy: part of a county overseen by a peasant Village Headsman, with outlying hamlets.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Hierarchies

summary: The days of labor service every peasant household owes each year for roads, walls, dykes and other public works, called by the Ministry of Works.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Works

summary: The anti-corruption rule at city gates: a sashed tariff inspector assesses goods but never touches money, and a licensor collects the posted rate without discretion.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of Revenue

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (stalwart; guards the Kaiu Wall against the Shadowlands). Families: Hida, Yasuki, Kaiu, Kuni, Hiruma. Patron Fortunes: Bishamon and Ebisu, so every Crab city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (refined; the Wasp's patrons). Families: Doji, Daidoji, Kakita, Asahina. Patron Fortunes: Benten and Daikoku, so every Crane city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (enigmatic). Families: Togashi, Mirumoto, Agasha, Kitsuki. Patron Fortunes: Hotei and Ebisu, so every Dragon city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (militant). Families: Akodo, Matsu, Ikoma, Kitsu. Patron Fortunes: Bishamon and Daikoku, so every Lion city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (spiritual). Families: Shiba, Isawa, Asako. Patron Fortunes: Fukurokujin and Hotei, so every Phoenix city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (underhanded; Tsuruchi's birth clan). Families: Bayushi, Shosuro, Soshi, Yogo. Patron Fortunes: Benten and Jurojin, so every Scorpion city has a temple to each.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the 7 Great Clans (nomadic). Families: Shinjo, Otaku, Moto, Ide, Iuchi. Patron Fortunes: Fukurokujin and Jurojin, so every Unicorn city has a temple to each. They shifted west to rule Medin al Salaat for some 700 years and returned about 200 years ago, warring on the clans that had taken their lands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of romantic love. Patron of the Crane and Scorpion clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of strength. Patron of the Crab and Lion clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of wealth. Patron of the Crane and Lion clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of honest work. Patron of the Crab and Dragon clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of wisdom and mercy. Patron of the Phoenix and Unicorn clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of contentment. Patron of the Dragon and Phoenix clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: One of the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck: the Fortune of longevity. Patron of the Scorpion and Unicorn clans.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: The seven Major Fortunes of good luck the Shinsei identified: Benten (romantic love), Bishamon (strength), Daikoku (wealth), Ebisu (honest work), Fukurokujin (wisdom and mercy), Hotei (contentment), Jurojin (longevity). Each Great Clan has two as its patrons: Crab Bishamon and Ebisu; Crane Benten and Daikoku; Dragon Hotei and Ebisu; Lion Bishamon and Daikoku; Phoenix Fukurokujin and Hotei; Scorpion Benten and Jurojin; Unicorn Fukurokujin and Jurojin.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: The Fortune of rice and of foxes; Fox rice is prized for offerings at Inari shrines.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > The Fox Clan > The Fox Clan's economy

summary: The Lord of Storms, known to sink ships weighed down by heavy sins; father of Hida Kaimetsu-Uo, who founded the Mantis Clan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Wasp Bounty Hunters Campaign > Bounties > Example bounties

summary: Rokugan's divinely ordained caste system, headed by the Hantei Emperor as the Son of Heaven. Samurai are the ruling caste and the only ones with full personhood ("people"); heimin are "half-people"; hinin are "non-people", the lowest of them burakumin. Monks stand outside it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Castes

summary: The ruling caste ("those who make war" or "those who serve"), about 2% of the population; mostly bushi (warriors), with some courtiers and samurai merchants. Only samurai are "people" in the Celestial Order.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Castes

summary: A samurai warrior; about 80% of samurai are bushi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > The Median Domain

summary: The "half-people" caste: farmers, merchants and craftspeople (carpenters, smiths, brewers, weavers, sword polishers and the like).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Castes

summary: The "non-people" caste: laborers, servants, porters, entertainers, beggars, criminals and the bankrupt. Its lowest part are the burakumin.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Castes

summary: The "untouchables" of the hinin caste who do ritually unclean work: tanners, butchers, cremators, morticians, night-soil handlers (owaiya), torturers and executioners of non-samurai.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Castes

summary: Rokugan's gold coin, and the amount of rice to feed a man for a year (about 40 gallons); by Imperial decree a koku coin and 40 gallons of rice are always equal for rent and taxes. 1 koku = 10 bu = 100 zeni = 1,000 sen.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Money

summary: A silver coin worth a tenth of a koku (10 zeni).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Money

summary: A copper coin worth a tenth of a bu (10 sen).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Money

summary: The smallest copper piece, a tenth of a zeni, minted in strings of ten that can be broken to make change.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Money

summary: A peasant merchant dynasty, named after its current patriarch ("the Masahito merchant family") because peasants may not keep a family name without a daimyo's dispensation. Most own farmland worked by tenant farmers.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Merchant Families

summary: Peasant militia: one male from many farming families trains monthly. "Licensed" ashigaru have proved good enough to carry peasant weapons unsupervised; "unlicensed" ashigaru have not.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Ashigaru

summary: The monk of a village district, keeping its birth, death, marriage and travel records; equivalent to an Adept Monk.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Monks

summary: The head of an Order's temple in a county town; equivalent to a Senior Monk.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Monks

summary: The head of an Order in a domain capital (an Abbot heads it in a province). The Fox call theirs a High Monk.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Monks

summary: From lowest: Initiate, Novice, Acolyte, Junior Monk, Adept Monk (a Country Monk), Senior Monk (a town Preceptor), Steward, Abbot, Grand Abbot. Monks stand outside the Celestial Order.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Monks

summary: About once a week, when farmers from across a county come to its town to buy, sell and barter; acting troupes earn most of their money then.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Entertainers

summary: A county's band of 5-10 entertainers (actors, jugglers, musicians) who play on market day and tour the villages.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Entertainers

summary: Mostly peasants with day jobs who steal or rob on the side; the strongest lead gangs of 4-8 that attack travelers and caravans. "Kage" (shadow) is a common bandit alias.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Bandits

summary: Heretical blood magic, powered by the names of the practitioner's victims; the more famous the name, the stronger. Practitioners carry the Shadowlands taint.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Maho-tsukai

summary: A witch who practices maho. Covens are usually 3-10 poor peasants; a powerful one who spreads their name violently takes the surname Jama.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Maho-tsukai

summary: A maho-tsukai who has learned to conceal the Shadowlands taint in their body.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Maho-tsukai

summary: A Kuni Witch Hunter of the Office of the Jade Champion, who hunts tsukai and bloodspeakers; most domain capitals have one (the notes give both about 200 and about 300 Empire-wide). Trained by childhood exposure to the taint, they can sometimes detect even a hidden taint. They swear a vow of poverty (gifts stay with the office) and use a false name so maho cannot use their true one.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Maho-tsukai

summary: Cunning, fierce creatures that cross into Rokugan over the Kaiu Wall or through the Burning Sands; they hide in the countryside stealing food, alone or in pairs. About 1% are man-eaters who seek strong victims.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Ogres

summary: The charter defining the duties of Imperial magistrates.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Imperials

summary: The Emperor's armies under the Shogun, manned by samurai from the clans and led mostly by Imperials (especially the Seppun). The 1st guards the Gateway to the Burning Sands, the 2nd Beiden Pass, the 3rd and most of the rest the Kaiu Wall.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Imperials

summary: The great wall guarding the Empire from the Shadowlands, held by the Crab Clan with over 20 Imperial legions.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > The Ministry of War

summary: The Hantei (the Emperor's family), Seppun, Otomo and Miya, who directly administer a small part of northeastern Rokugan and staff Imperial posts.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Clan Populations

summary: Small clans outside the 7 Great Clans: the Mantis (largest), Dragonfly, Fox, Sparrow, Wasp, Tortoise and Hare, among others.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Clan Populations

summary: A senior vassal house of one of the largest Families, its domain comparable to the ruling daimyo's, with special military or administrative duties (the Akito of the Hida, the Tsume of the Doji, the Damasu of the Akodo).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Clan Populations

summary: A city found suitable for the Emperor to hold Imperial Winter Court; a "Shiro" lacks that designation, and "Shinden" (temple) marks a capital known chiefly for its temples.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Large Cities

summary: The Imperial capital and largest city, about a million inhabitants.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Large Cities

summary: The second-largest city (about 500,000), the Scorpion trading hub south of Beiden Pass, held by the Michio house of the Shosuro; also called Kyuden Michio.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Large Cities

summary: The third-largest city (over 300,000), capital of the Lion's Damasu house and fought over in the Lion/Crane war; also called Kyuden Damasu.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Large Cities

summary: The Crab's great harbor city on Earthquake Bay (about 250,000), never granted Kyuden status because the Crane hold a grudge over the Yasuki leaving them. The PCs' predecessors were promoted to be Marshals there.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Large Cities

summary: The coming-of-age ceremony at 14, when a samurai becomes a legal adult and often chooses an adult name.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > The Median Domain

summary: About 90% of farmers work land owned by merchant families or samurai, paying rent while the landowner pays the tax; the landowner is said to have "authority over" so many households.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Setting > Village Headsmen

summary: A lineage tied to one province it has administered for generations (the Aki lineage and Akishi province of the Daidoji); a province held that way is a "dynasty province". Hachinaga was the Shin lineage's dynasty province.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Samurai Lineages > Provincial and cosmopolitan lineages

summary: A lineage based in its domain's capital rather than tied to a province, often holding a traditional post (the Sasara lineage of the Ryusei always holds Minister of Rites). Provinces governed by appointment on merit and politics are "stewardship provinces".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Samurai Lineages > Provincial and cosmopolitan lineages

summary: A lineage's representative on its house chancellery, who also runs the lineage's voluntary support fund and makes patronage visible by naming who paid for a kinsman's advancement.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Samurai Lineages > Lineage Patronage and Mutual Aid

summary: An office's right to a share of the taxes it collects: a daimyo, governor or county magistrate pays samurai stipends out of the tax-farming cut at their own level, and keeps what is left over after meeting their obligation.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Structure of Rokugani Government > Samurai Lineages > Lineage Patronage and Mutual Aid

summary: Lady Doji's rules for what samurai of different ranks owe one another and the lower castes: clothing, bowing, hospitality, seating and gifts. A samurai's stipend is the square of their rank in koku, and a gift's value goes by the highest rank involved.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank > Gifts and the Accordances of Rank

summary: Two samurai within 3 formal ranks of each other are of accordant standing (otherwise "discordant"); within 1 rank, adjusted for merits, they are of peer standing. Accordant standing is needed to share a small table or to interview someone; peer standing to arrest them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank > The Doctrine of Three Steps

summary: A duel challenge on valid grounds. It must be accepted from an equal or higher-ranked bushi or a lower-ranked one of peer standing; a challenger more than 3 formal ranks below may be dismissed (the challenged is "beyond the reach" of them).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank > The Doctrine of Three Steps

summary: The legal standard (from Soshi Saibankan) for weighing merits when judging peer standing: the magistrate may consider anything relevant.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Measure of Standing and the Accordances of Rank > The Doctrine of Three Steps

summary: A 360-day year of twelve 30-day lunar months, starting on the first day of spring (early February); the full moon falls on the 15th. Each month has a zodiac animal and a traditional name: 1 Hare (Mutsuki), 2 Dragon (Kisaragi), 3 Serpent (Yayoi), 4 Horse (Uzuki), 5 Goat (Satsuki), 6 Monkey (Minazuki), 7 Rooster (Fumizuki), 8 Dog (Hazuki), 9 Boar (Nagatsuki), 10 Rat (Kaminazuki), 11 Ox (Shimotsuki), 12 Tiger (Shiwasu).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Twelve Months

summary: The day is divided into twelve two-hour "hours" named for the zodiac: Hare 6-8am, Dragon, Serpent, Horse (noon-2pm), Goat, Monkey, Rooster, Dog, Boar, Rat (midnight-2am), Ox, Tiger.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Twelve Hours of the Day

summary: The 60-year cycle naming each year (and day) by one of the Ten Heavenly Stems and one of the Twelve Earthly Branches (the zodiac animals), e.g. the Yang Wood Rat.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Sexagenary Cycle

summary: One of the three 10-day thirds of a month (upper, middle, lower); the last day of a month is misoka, the last of the year oomisoka.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Twelve Months

summary: Rokugan's staples: rice (above all), wheat or barley, soybeans, azuki beans and millet. Domains are measured by rice production.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > Crops and Farming Seasons

summary: Festival: the New Year festival filling the first 15 days of the 1st month; cooking is taboo, so special foods are prepared ahead, and the year's "firsts" are celebrated together.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 1st day of the year (about 4 February): rituals, then a night festival of parades, fireworks and hot sweet sake; everyone counts themselves a year older.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 5th day of the 1st month, when new ranks are bestowed on those promoted.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 7th day of the 1st month (a Gosechi holiday): a soup of the seven spring herbs.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 15th day of the 1st month, the end of Oshogatsu: rice porridge, and New Year decorations burned to send the visiting kami home.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 18th day of the 1st month: an archery contest between the Inner and Outer Palace Guards; also held by cities, and used to settle points in the Lion/Crane peace talks.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 1st Month: Mutsuki ("affection month")

summary: Festival: the 4th day of the 2nd month, when the Ministries of Rites call the Rice God down from the hills.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 2nd Month: Kisaragi ("changing")

summary: Festival: a seven-day Shinseist festival around the Vernal Equinox (2nd month, days 12-18): families tend ancestors' graves and attend daily temple services.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 2nd Month: Kisaragi ("changing")

summary: Festival: the 3rd day of the 3rd month (a Gosechi holiday): straw dolls carry away impurity into rivers; a powerful day for maho.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 3rd Month: Yayoi ("new life")

summary: Festival: the 7th day of the 4th month: horseback archery and a shrine procession.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 4th Month: Uzuki ("unohana" or "deutzia")

summary: Festival: the 5th day of the 5th month (a Gosechi holiday): horse races and archery against roaming evil spirits; five-color silk amulets and iris garlands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 5th Month: Satsuki ("sprout")

summary: Festival: the 10th-30th of the 5th month, when the Emperor and daimyo give alms of rice and salt.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 5th Month: Satsuki ("sprout")

summary: Festival: the eve of a new season: the Autumn Setsubun (6th month, 30th day) is a day of reckoning when debts are settled and the Emperor performs the Oharae, the Great Purification; the Spring Setsubun is New Year's Eve (12th month, 30th day).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 6th Month: Minazuki ("dry")

summary: Festival: the 7th day of the 7th month (a Gosechi holiday): stargazing for the lovers the Weaver Maiden and the Cowherd.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 7th Month: Fumizuki ("poetry")

summary: Festival: the 15th day of the 7th month, when ancestors' spirits are invited home for a day and a night; masked dancing under lanterns.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 7th Month: Fumizuki ("poetry")

summary: Festival: a seven-day Shinseist festival around the Autumnal Equinox (8th month, from the 12th).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 8th Month: Hazuki ("leaf")

summary: Festival: the 15th day of the 8th month: the best night for moon viewing, and the Great Liberation, when animals are released at shrines.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 8th Month: Hazuki ("leaf")

summary: Festival: the 9th day of the 9th month, the last Gosechi holiday: chrysanthemum displays and chrysanthemum wine for long life.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 9th Month: Nagatsuki ("long")

summary: Festival: the first Day of the Boar in the 10th month: seven piglet rice cakes for good fortune.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 10th Month: Kaminazuki ("no gods")

summary: Festival: the 4th day of the 11th month: thanks for the harvest; new rice is not eaten before it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 11th Month: Shimotsuki ("frost")

summary: The five great seasonal festivals on "double odd" days: Nanakusa (1/7), Hinamatsuri (3/3), the Iris Festival (5/5), Tanabata (7/7) and the Chrysanthemum Festival (9/9).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar

summary: The season when a daimyo (or the Emperor, at a Kyuden) hosts guests through the snowbound months; guests arrive by Shousetsu in the 10th month. Winter Court 1129 was at Ryoko Owari.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Rokugan's Calendar > The Festival Calendar > 10th Month: Kaminazuki ("no gods")

summary: A promise sworn BY a god, so the person it was sworn to can release you; oaths of office end with the office. A vow is sworn TO a god, and only the god can release you. Both begin by the swearer naming themselves unambiguously, then the god, then the promise.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: A promise sworn TO a Fortune (or other divine being), binding until the god releases you. Swearing gains no favor in itself; living by it does, and breaking it brings misfortune, so a vow must be hard enough to matter but not so hard it is broken. The Fortune, not the swearer, judges whether it is broken. Lifetime vows and limited (task) vows both exist.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: A kind of vow: the commonest vow: orienting one's whole life around one Fortune until death; mostly monks and priests, but also e.g. a duelist to Bishamon or a magistrate to Yozo.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: renouncing wealth in one of several forms (an official whose gifts stay with the office; a pilgrim with no more than 1 koku and one of any item).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: a vow of "truth-speaking": never to tell a lie for any reason, though technically true but misleading statements are allowed.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: a limited vow to see that a shrine, temple or other work is built.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: a limited vow, usually to Hofukushu, to make one's life about achieving a particular vengeance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: a Lion vow to Emma-O by the deeply disgraced: to seek a useful death in battle for their daimyo; deathseekers gather in Deathseeker platoons.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A kind of vow: usually to Yozo: to bring about the just outcome regardless of anything else, even against a higher authority.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: Further kinds of vow: pilgrimage, offering, pacifism, non-killing, prayer, fasting, matchmaking, atonement, obedience (acolytes), celibacy, silence, bloodlessness (vegetarian), isolation, charity, discovery.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A journey of training, often in self-imposed exile, usually under vows to Bishamon; Matsu Hitomi's book "Vengeance and Justice" is its foundational text.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A Lion samurai who avenged her brother after a long warrior's pilgrimage and wrote "Vengeance and Justice"; Hitomi is a common adult name for women seeking revenge.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: The current daimyo of the Mirumoto Family (Dragon), who took the name vowing vengeance on Hida Yakamo for her brother and cut off his hand.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: A storyteller of three centuries ago, falsely exiled, who won Benten's favor on pilgrimage and became the Imperial Matchmaker; wrote "Benten's Blessing" and is the subject of the classic play "Doji Shizue and the Secrets of Calligraphy".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Benten's Blessing

summary: All the Fortunes (a large but finite number); the Seven Fortunes of Good Luck are the best known. A human may "become" a Fortune after death by merging with one that already existed, recognized or elevated by the Emperor.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > On Vows to the Fortunes

summary: The younger Fortune of vengeance: legal retribution imposed by a judge, and penance.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: The elder Fortune of vengeance: personal, sacrificial revenge; Witch Hunters swear their vow of poverty to him.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: The Fortune of magistrates and judges and of "preventative justice": Soshi Saibankan, who in life wrote the Emerald Charter and established Rokugan's common law of precedent; Imperial magistrates are "Saibankan's net".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Soshi Saibankan

summary: The Fortune of roads and orderly travel, said to sit at Daikoku's right hand; his Order of the Barefoot Brethren walk the roads carrying messages.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Fortune of the west wind, bringer of opportunity that must be fought for.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Fortune of the east wind: knowledge, justice and travel toward civilization.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Fortune of death.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > Vengeance and Justice

summary: The Fortune of loyalty and honor.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Fortune of travel.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Fortune of fishermen.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Soothsaying

summary: Amaterasu, the Sun, ancestor of the Hantei; she stands for harmony. Oaths are sworn "in the light of our radiant Lady Sun".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The Moon, who delights in conflict and in individuals pursuing their own ambitions regardless of cost; those who pray to him often are distrusted. Served by a heavenly court and a secret Order of Lord Moon.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: A centuries-old secret society sworn to Lord Moon, whose members keep each other's identities secret and pursue their own ambitions; the PCs of the Karmic Inquisitors campaign belonged to it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: The fungal blight that destroyed over half the Damasu domain's rice and soybean crop in 1129, with none of the expected omens; investigating it was the Karmic Inquisitors campaign.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows

summary: A great Phoenix shugenja-scholar of centuries past who summoned the oni lord that became the hidden Great Library, published its books as his own, practiced maho without losing his powers, and achieved immortality. His books carry a disclaimer ordering reports to the Jade Champion.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > On Vows to the Fortunes

summary: An oni lord (Oni no Akuma) in the form of a library hidden in the Isawa Woodlands, said to hold everything ever written and more; it cannot be found the same way twice.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > On Vows to the Fortunes

summary: The Imperial official who hunts maho and forbidden lore; currently Kuni Utagu, after Kuni Yori was executed in 1127.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Oaths and Vows > On Vows to the Fortunes

summary: A domain's network of temples, monasteries and shrines to one Fortune ("the Order of Bishamon"); its capital temple is the sovereign temple under a Grand Abbot, with subordinate temples under provincial Abbots, town monasteries under Preceptors and village shrines under Country Monks.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization

summary: A state (not a sin) that must be purified before entering a shrine or temple. Fish is clean; pork or poultry needs a purifying bath; rabbit, venison or sheep a shrine cleansing; horse or cattle leaves one unclean for over a month. Ritually slaughtered goat is "mountain tuna".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Temple Organization > Food Purity

summary: Literally "truth-speaking", colloquially predicting the future. Two categories: augury (reading universal omens - fortunetelling for a person, divination for a region) and prophecy (god-given sight - wisdom prophecy and covenant prophecy). The foundational text is "On Soothsaying".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Soothsaying

summary: Prophecy from a compact with a god: a sentinel prophecy (the god warns of a threat, as Osano-Wo reddens the dawn sky before fires in Komori) or a stratagem prophecy (the god shares a plan for mortals to carry out).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Soothsaying

summary: Kitsu Okura's survey, in "On the Relationship between Man and the Fortunes", of six explanations for why the Fortunes do not speak clearly - all wrong, he says, but each holding a glimpse of truth.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > On the Relationship between Man and the Fortunes

summary: The underworld, where most souls descend after death.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes

summary: The realm of the honored dead.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Between Places

summary: Places that coexist in two locations or realms: the Shinomen Forest opening into the Isawa Woodlands, the Shifting Islands, and most dangerously the Forgotten Tomb, which exists in both the mortal world and Yomi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Between Places

summary: The cataclysm of 1123, in this setting a coup by a cult of Lord Moon against several Great Clans and the Emperor's authority; Bayushi Shoju was murdered, the Thunders defeated the moon cultist Shinjo Jotsu, and Jama no Iuchiban Kohaku slew the remaining Thunders. Since then it is heretical to pray to Lord Moon inside a temple consecrated to Lady Sun.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > 3rd Imperial Legion Backstories > Isawa Koichi

summary: Corruption from the Shadowlands or from maho; the body can expel a little, but enough settles in permanently. It is hateful to the elemental kami, so a shugenja who takes it loses their powers.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > 3rd Imperial Legion Backstories

summary: General of the 3rd Imperial Legion on the Kaiu Wall, who believes he is destined to face overwhelming Shadowlands forces a third time and so will not travel home.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > 3rd Imperial Legion Backstories > Matsu Tsutomu

summary: A Kuni shugenja and former Jade Champion, executed in 1127 for high treason (experimenting with moon cultists and maho).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > 3rd Imperial Legion Backstories

summary: A legendary artifact, said to be the marriage contract of Lord Moon and Lady Sun: whoever sees it learns a terrible truth that always comes to pass. Yasuki Noriko saw it foretell the execution of the Sato lineage. It is kept in the Forgotten Tomb; no Hantei has looked on it since the 16th.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > The Burning Words

summary: The Hantei's religious order of Lady Sun, which investigates threats to the Emperor and can make the rare holy incense used in place of "fate tying".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Moto Khuyag's Death Detectors

summary: An ancient, disfavored (never banned) divination that ties the fate of someone already sentenced to die to an unrelated question.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Moto Khuyag's Death Detectors

summary: A 300-year-old smuggling syndicate of ex-legionnaires beside the 1st Imperial Legion that trades silk to gaijin for silver and supplies the Imperial Mint; it also tends the 11 Imperial gardens of Chai Sedo through the "Western Star" mining company. Its leaders were the PCs of the Hidden Way campaign.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Moto Khuyag's Death Detectors

summary: The 1st Imperial Legion's post at the Gateway to the Burning Sands, with its shrine (abbot Toranosuke) and 11 Imperial gardens, each kept by a "Master of Purity".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Moto Khuyag's Death Detectors

summary: Hantei Fukuhachi, the Emperor's second son and General of the 1st Imperial Legion, which the second son traditionally commands.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > 1st Imperial Legion Backstories

summary: The Moto daimyo, waging the Emperor's campaign to bring gaijin lands (the Uru, Medin al Salaat) under Imperial control.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Moto Khuyag's Death Detectors

summary: A fox who chewed her own name away to escape her husband Takaba's wards and became a being that eats names; whoever she eats is forgotten by the world and the world adjusts (she ate the Yasuki daimyo Kiringu, so his brother Tsanumi led the Yasuki out of the Crane). Imprisoned in the Forgotten Tomb until Moto Tsume's attack freed her.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > The Nameless One

summary: Harm from a spirit encounter that weakens a person's ties to their clan, family or allies, real but too subtle to prove.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Connection Damage

summary: An elemental spirit corrupted by anger or a past wrong.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Connection Damage > The Armor of Fool's Regret

summary: A mischievous spirit that afflicts people and animals, e.g. tormenting dreams.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Connection Damage > Otaku Mirai

summary: A famous sword, "Wind Blowing Down the Mountain", that helped slay the Maw; said to want to strike downhill. Kept by the Kitsuki Family.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Connection Damage > Yamaoroshi

summary: A great Shadowlands monster that destroyed most of Hiruma lands before it was slain at the Battle of the Cresting Wave.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Fortunes > Connection Damage > Yamaoroshi

summary: The seven outlawed disciplines Witch Hunters watch for: Shadowlands taint magic, name magic, wound magic, summoning (oni, mujina, kansen, zombies, ghosts), crafting (obsidian blades, totems), dark divination (learning a named person's fears, desires and regrets) and fleshshaping. Taking a name means asking for it three times and being answered.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers

summary: A demon summoned from Jigoku by maho; it needs a name to exist in this realm, so summoning one takes a weighty name, much blood and taint, usually a whole coven. Jama Kyoso discovered how to dismiss and recall them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama no Iuchiban Kyoso

summary: The sorcerers of Medin al Salaat, who practice fleshshaping and the removal of their own hearts.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers

summary: A samurai name is "<Family> no <House> <personal>": Akodo no Sugiwara Natsuki is of the Sugiwara house of the Akodo Family. "no" (of) is usually omitted for the ruling house, and the Family is often dropped informally ("Seri Go"). A Jama name puts the teacher in the house position: Jama no Iuchiban Kohaku was taught by Iuchiban.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants

summary: Hantei Iuchiban, an Emperor's second son about 600 years ago who learned maho while commanding the 1st Imperial Legion, invented the concealment of the taint (the first bloodspeaker) and the Jama name, and attempted a coup; killed, imprisoned in the Forgotten Tomb, resurrected, killed again, and now sealed in the Tomb of Iuchiban built by Kaiu Gineza.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants

summary: The name taken by Iuchiban's followers and, after them, powerful maho-tsukai, a perversion of a samurai family name.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants

summary: A bloodspeaker: once Shiba no Iga Suru, who brought Iuchiban his first maho texts; impersonates traveling samurai to trade political help for names; resurrected Iuchiban.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama no Iuchiban Suru

summary: A bloodspeaker: an old peasant witch, "the dark daughter of Fu Leng", who first taught Iuchiban; lives in the Shadowlands and baits Crab armies into spreading her name.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama Musume

summary: A bloodspeaker: the smith who perfected maho crafting and made the four Bloodswords (Ambition, Revenge, Judgement, Passion); still makes obsidian weapons for bloodspeakers.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Asahina Yajinden

summary: A bloodspeaker: "queen of oni", who showed that oni need names and discovered summoning with a dying victim's name and dismissing and recalling oni.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama no Iuchiban Kyoso

summary: A bloodspeaker: a monk turned bloodspeaker who learned the khadi secrets, taught countless peasant covens to hide the taint, blasted the Kaiu Wall open for the Maw, rebuilt Iuchiban's body, and slew the surviving Thunders on the Day of Thunder.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama no Iuchiban Kohaku

summary: A bloodspeaker: Kohaku's apprentice, who cursed recovered ancestral swords and summoned a rust oni that ruined every sword of the army sent against it.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban and His Lieutenants > Jama no Kohaku Hoshiko

summary: A past cabal of five families that controlled the Imperial Chancellery: the Isawa, the Doji, the Tsume house, the Bayushi and the Michio house. Broken up by Hantei the 16th.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban's Coup History > The Gozoku

summary: "The Steel Chrysanthemum", the Emperor who broke the Gozoku by ruthless means, including turning Witch Hunters on his enemies (whose excesses led to their reforms); he elevated Daidoji Tojo to be the Fortune of Dung.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Maho and Bloodspeakers > Iuchiban's Coup History > Hantei the 16th

summary: A samurai priest who calls on the elemental kami (air, earth, fire, water); about 1 samurai in 10,000, so half of domains have none, and magistrates go to great lengths not to deprive a daimyo of theirs. Shugenja are kept away from duels. Maho destroys their powers.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Shugenja

summary: The Council of Elemental Masters, who rule the Isawa Family (Phoenix) and have the final word in Phoenix affairs; Isawa no Naka Kuro, the Grand Master of the Elements, is an immortal shugenja.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > Shugenja

summary: The vassal domain of the Akodo Family (Lion) whose capital is Toshi Ranbo; setting of the Karmic Inquisitors and First Toshi Ranbo campaigns. Taken by the Tsume in 1117, retaken by the Lion in 1121, struck by the kumosaya blight in 1129.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign

summary: Monks of the Order of Bishamon in Toshi Ranbo tasked with finding the sin behind the kumosaya blight; the PCs of that campaign, secretly also members of the Order of Lord Moon.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Campaign Description

summary: Master of the Lunar Way ("Master of the Way"), head of the Order of Lord Moon; by day Warden of the Five Gates of the Temple of Bishamon.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > "the Order"

summary: Seeker of the Moon's Chosen ("the Seeker") of the Order of Lord Moon, who finds recruits.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > "the Order"

summary: Teacher of the Astral Ways ("the Teacher") of the Order of Lord Moon, and Herald of the Bell of the Temple of Bishamon.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > "the Order"

summary: Steward of the Sacred Cache ("the Steward") of the Order of Lord Moon, who hides its ritual implements.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > "the Order"

summary: A prophet who drew huge peasant crowds and revealed in 1120 that the Day of Thunder was at hand; murdered at the order of Shinjo Jotsu. The Baitenist movement grew from his followers.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: An Imperial magistrate secretly heir to the moon cult, who had Baiten murdered and was defeated by the Seven Thunders on the Day of Thunder (1123).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: An Imperial magistrate who defended Baiten, was made ronin for striking Prince Fukuhachi, became the Unicorn Thunder and was slain by Jama Kohaku; his name was restored after death.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: General of the Northern Armies of the Crane, who held Toshi Ranbo in 1118 (killing Akodo Arasou); murdered in 1120 by the bloodspeaker Jama Manabu, whose oni then ravaged the city.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: Daimyo of the Lion Clan since his brother Akodo Arasou died assaulting Toshi Ranbo in 1118; retook the city in 1121.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: The office created to hunt moon cultists, headed by Prince Hantei Daigotsu (the Emperor's second son) with Matsu Gohei; its Crystal Charter is not yet written. Its test burns out an eye with sunlight through crystal - a moon cultist's eye blackens throughout.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: "The butcher", a Lion commander notorious in the Lion/Crane war, who later hunted moon cultists in Toshi Ranbo with the Crystal Champion.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: Dark artifacts opened and recharged at the Forgotten Tomb in 1127; the Crab, under the Kuni Witch Hunters, began experimenting with them in 1128.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: Scorpion lord who thwarted the moon cultists who murdered his brother, the daimyo Bayushi Shoju, in 1123, and later married Shoju's widow Bayushi Kachiko.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: Daimyo of the Unicorn Clan since 1124, when he executed the moon cultist Shinjo Yokatsu; also executed Iuchi Daiyu after Iuchi Shahai's attempt on the Emperor in 1127.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: A moon cultist who tried to assassinate the Emperor at the Imperial Winter Court at Kyuden Shinjo (1127) and escaped; her coven is still at large.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline
