summary: Daimyo of the Crab Clan, wounded on the Day of Thunder, when his eldest daughter Hida O-Ushi, the Crab Thunder, was killed.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Karmic Inquisitors Timeline

summary: The celestial servants of Lord Moon whose disciples the Order of Lord Moon become: Ryoshun the Guardian, Nanube the Deceiver, Goju the Hunter and Suro the Thief. Discipleship grows in three phases - Crescent, Half and Gibbous Moon; a Gibbous Moon disciple fails the crystal test, a Crescent Moon disciple passes.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Lord Moon's Heavenly Court

summary: A servant of Lord Moon, the Guardian or the Protector, who guards the threshold between the celestial heavens and the mortal realm (the star at the top of the night sky); he brought Lord Moon's court into Toshi Ranbo through a bargain with the Imperial magistrate Yasuki Suzuki.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Lord Moon's Heavenly Court

summary: A servant of Lord Moon, the Deceiver or the Liar, who Lord Moon's court entertainer, whose lies forge bonds truth cannot; her disciples use deception to take control of social situations.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Lord Moon's Heavenly Court

summary: A servant of Lord Moon, the Hunter or the Tracker, who who chased down the spirits that fled their names; his disciples see all things in and out of their place and can find people whose names they know.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Lord Moon's Heavenly Court

summary: A servant of Lord Moon, the Thief or the Taker, who who stole the Shadow of Nothing and can go unseen; the Scorpion Thunder Shosuro is said to have taken her name from him.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > Lord Moon's Heavenly Court

summary: Daimyo of the Damasu since the Lion retook Toshi Ranbo; she was on the Imperial Chancellery when most of her family died in 1117. Married to Akodo Hiroki, Akodo Toturi's cousin. Wields Amatsukami no Ken.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Lineages > The Damasu lineage

summary: The seven lineages on the Damasu chancellery: Damasu (ruling, rebuilt from survivors and newcomers), Chura (Yamagata province), Hiyu (Suruga), Sei (Shimotsuke, founded by Chancellor Akodo no Damasu Sei), and the old cosmopolitan Kiyomi (always Minister of Justice), Bian and Uyo. Smaller: Riori (Owari, a thousand years), Taizo (Izumo, disgraced for mocking Baiten), Nire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Lineages

summary: The six original provinces - Owari ("tail-end", the old Crane border, held by the Riori), Mino ("beautiful swamp"), Bizen (the canal to the Drowned Merchant River), Hitachi (country estates, including Hikobayashi county), Higo and Izumo (cloud-watching soothsayers) - plus three won from the Tsume: Yamagata, Suruga and Shimotsuke. Tango was lost to Shitsuten in the treaty duels.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Provinces

summary: The dueling tournament under the Lion/Crane peace treaty (1128) in which 20 Lion duelists faced Crane and Phoenix duelists to decide four disputed provinces.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Provinces

summary: The sovereign temple of the Order of Bishamon in Toshi Ranbo, over 200 monks, one of the largest in the Empire (Grand Abbot Goemon; relics kept by Steward Iori). Its relics include the Staff of Bishamon, the Pillar of Ten Thousand Names, the Prayer Beads of the Guardian Spirits, the Sword of the First Vow, the Helm of Discerning Valor, the Eternal Wisdom Tree and the Chamber of Celestial Echoes; the Tsume took the Tooth of the Shinsei, the Jade Shinsei and the Chime of Harmony.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Temples

summary: Head of the Order of Daikoku in Scorpion lands, a prophet revealed on the Day of Thunder as the descendant of the Shinsei, who gathered the Seven Thunders; killed on the Day of Thunder. He popularized the vow of charity.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Temples > The Temple of Daikoku

summary: The Fortune of artists and entertainers; the Order of Sadahako carried on the prophet Baiten's ministry and is the fastest-growing order in the Empire.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Damasu Temples > The Temple of Sadahako

summary: The minor Fortune of sensei (teachers).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign

summary: The highest commendation for anyone below the rank of daimyo, awarded by the Imperial Ministry of Retainers; given to the Heroes of the Black Scrolls (among them Kuni Isamu, Shiba Asayo and Kitsuki Fu).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign

summary: Daimyo of the Crab Clan after Mirumoto Hitomi cut off Hida Yakamo's right hand at the Hollyhock Festival; Hida Kisada's acknowledged daughter.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign

summary: A famous sword: the ancestral sword of the Damasu, given to Akodo Damasu in a trance; held by Damasu Chiho.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Amatsukami no Ken

summary: A famous sword: the Riori sword of the governors of Owari, which pierces armor like a needle.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Ohari

summary: A famous sword: a sword blessed by the Jade Dragon that whispers guidance, pushing its wielders against the Shadowlands; held by Akodo no Damasu Kaguya.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Seishinsho

summary: A famous sword: a sword of Lion family unity commissioned by Akodo Fujita; carried by Akodo no Damasu Sei.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Kishin no Ketsui

summary: A famous sword: Matsu Yokijiro's sword, which must accept any challenge to the death and pass to whoever kills its wielder in a duel.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Akuzuki

summary: A famous sword: the ancestral sword of the Tsume, which cleft a meteor; strongest on the attack; held by Doji no Tsume Takashi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Kasai Tsume

summary: A famous sword: one of Hyobu's seven swords from a silver dragon's scale, blinding the wicked; wielded by Mirumoto Kiyoshi, "the Silver Streak of Justice".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Seiginryu

summary: A famous sword: the feared Scorpion sword that anchors the souls of those it kills for binding in Traitor's Grove; wielded by Bayushi no Akiko Maiko.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Tamashikari

summary: The cursed sword "Lost Heaven", the swordsmith Daidoji Masamune's last, forged in hatred of the Yasuki; once drawn it must take a life. Taken from Shinden Asahina and used by Doji Masayo to win Tango province in the Sunset Blade Trials.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Shitsuten

summary: A Scorpion grove made by Soshi shugenja where executed traitors' souls are bound to trees and kept from rebirth.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Tamashikari

summary: A large Yasuki harbor town on Earthquake Bay (not actually a village), where the Yasuki Taka system was first used; home of Peddler's Row and the feared Lords of the Coin.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Karmic Inquisitors Campaign > The Damasu Domain > Famous Swords > Shitsuten

summary: The five Imperial magistrates Prince Fukuhachi appointed over Toshi Ranbo's five districts under Tsume occupation, hearing appeals together (the PCs of the First Toshi Ranbo campaign); its noted members included Shinjo Jotsu, Yasuki Suzuki and Otaku Taira.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign

summary: A capable, extraordinarily corrupt Tsume-era lieutenant and karo to Doji Kanroku who ran a criminal conspiracy in his district; later married Governor Tsume Momoko and died when the Lion retook the city.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign

summary: A district captain in occupied Toshi Ranbo, son of the Crane Champion, who lived simply beside his barracks and trusted Doji Hirota completely.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign

summary: Akodo no Damasu Atsumaru, the beloved former county magistrate of Hikobayashi who retired as a monk and kept settling peasants' disputes under the Tsume; later lobbied for the Damasu at Otosan Uchi.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > Hikobayashi County

summary: A newly formed minor clan, led by Niban, that accepts ronin and even raises wave men to the samurai caste.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > Nightingale Bushi

summary: Mirumoto Kiyoshi (blunt duelist), Togashi Ichiharu (enigmatic tattooed monk who answers with questions) and Kitsuki Hina (silent, highest-ranking, a hidden duelist): Dragon magistrates in Toshi Ranbo, nicknamed "the Dragon PCs".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > The Dragon Magistrates

summary: A famously righteous, harsh Lion duelist and teacher who wields Akuzuki and won Yamagata province against Doji Reju in the Sunset Blade Trials.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > Matsu Yokijiro

summary: Revered Sensei of the Lion and karo to Akodo Toturi, who planned the retaking of Toshi Ranbo with ninja infiltrators led by Matsu Hiroru (posing as the merchant Uhiro).

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > The Lion's Inside Plan

summary: Dangerous, skilled fighters (a profession) usually employed by large merchant houses as their best "mercenaries".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > The Lion's Inside Plan

summary: Grand Abbot of the Order of Sadahako in Crane lands, fiercely orthodox and provocative, brought to Toshi Ranbo after Baiten's banishment.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > Grand Abbot Benshi

summary: The river by Toshi Ranbo (linked to the city by canal) forming much of the old Lion border.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign

summary: A pleasure-loving Unicorn grain trader of the Dorai house (Firefly River Valley wheat) who has negotiated Toshi Ranbo's imports for decades.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The First Toshi Ranbo Campaign > Shinjo no Dorai Rakuo

summary: A campaign in which the PCs were licensed ashigaru from a farming village rising into the provincial city of Koishi (working at the Reflected Moon) and caravan work, using Profession rules instead of schools.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Peasant Campaign

summary: A peasant fighter-for-hire; also a profession whose abilities help in combat.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Peasant Campaign

summary: The legion guarding the Gateway to the Land of the Burning Sands, commanded by the Emperor's second son (now Prince Fukuhachi). Its postings count two ranks higher than a clan army's (other Imperial legions one), so they are highly sought.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The 1st Imperial Legion

summary: Legion > Battalion > Company > Platoon > Squad, led by a Legion General, Battalion Commander, Company Captain, Platoon Lieutenant and Squad Sergeant (with a Corporal). Above legions: an Army under an Army General, and titles like "General of the Southern Armies of the Crane".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The 1st Imperial Legion > Ranks in the Imperial legion

term: Gateway to the Land of the Burning Sands
summary: A 13-mile valley through the Twilight Mountains between Shinjo and Moto lands, with Chai Sedo at its north end and Outsider Keep (the Hidden Way's base, by an old silver mine) at its south; about 400 miles east of the actual desert.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The 1st Imperial Legion > The Gateway and Outsider Keep

summary: The mountains along Rokugan's entire western border.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign

summary: Foreigners outside the Empire. Trade with gaijin lands was banned by Imperial decree over 300 years ago.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > Gaijin

summary: A northern horse-riding tribe ("horse rider") that rebelled against the Moto; led by Timur Beg and backed by Medin al Salaat, they were warred on by Moto Gaheris.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > Gaijin

summary: The nearest gaijin city, about 400 miles into the Burning Sands: a caliphate under Caliph Hanan Talibah, with factions including the Almekhem, the Qabal of the Sahir (sorcerers), the khadi, the Nizari (assassins) and the Houses of Dahab (merchants). Ruled by the Unicorn for centuries; once Medinat al Salaam.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > Gaijin > Medin al Salaat

summary: The nomadic, horse-herding Unicorn family west of the Twilight Mountains, organized in "clans" (tribes) under khans, with Moto Gaheris as khan of khans and daimyo. Their capital is Shiro Moto (Karakoru). They pay taxes in horses, keep a secret law (the Yassa), and worship four Gods of Death.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto

summary: The Moto legal code, "secret writings" readable only by khans and their advisors so its letter cannot be abused; rulings set no precedent. Testimony is sworn by Hiderigami, the Fortune of drought.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > Moto Laws (the yassa)

summary: The four the Moto revere: Emma-O (the Fortune of death), Enma (guardian of the gates of Jigoku), King Yan (judge of souls, ruler of oni) and Wei Tin (lord of ghosts). Moto Gaheris carries a sword for each: Bloodstorm, Lamentation, Lightning, Retirement.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > The Gods of Death

summary: The southernmost Moto tribe, sworn to destroy Shadowlands creatures and the Dark Moto; their holy shrine is Bodi Kaikhan.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > The Vindicator Moto

summary: Skeletal riders of the Shadowlands led by Moto Tsume, once a Vindicator who sought immortality; they recruit dying Crab legionnaires, claiming to fight the oni lords. Bayushi Tangen named and described them.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > The Dark Moto

summary: A Scorpion warrior-poet who wrote the treatise "Lies" for the Emperor and "The Dark Moto".

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > Bayushi Tangen

summary: The great desert west and south of Moto lands, said to be scorched by Lady Sun; it bars the Shadowlands, since the taint travels through water.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > The Burning Sands Desert

summary: Four sounds like "death", so Rokugani avoid it: no trips on the 4th, no four-story buildings, and gifts of 4 coins get a lesser coin added; a gift of four of something is a threat.

source.section: L7R Campaign Notes > The Hidden Way Campaign > The Moto > The Gods of Death

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). A number of times per adventure equal to your rank in this knack, you may draw void from your surroundings and regain a spent void point. If you target a character when doing this, that character loses a void point; if that character has no void points then the next time they would regain one they do not.

source.section: School Knacks > Absorb Void

summary: School knack (Ring: varies). When performing physical actions which are not covered by skills (e.g. running, climbing, swimming, etc) everyone rolls (2 * Ring)k(Ring).

source.section: School Knacks > Athletics

summary: School knack (Ring: School Ring). You may ask the elemental spirits about events which they have recently witnessed. Spend a void point and roll this knack with your School Ring.

source.section: School Knacks > Commune

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). You receive 2X points per day, where X is equal to the rank of this knack. After you make any roll, you may spend up to X of these points to raise the roll by the number of points spent.

source.section: School Knacks > Conviction

summary: School knack (Ring: Fire). When an opponent attacks you, roll this knack to make an attack against them before they roll theirs. If you counterattack an attack directed at someone else, the TN is raised by 5 times the attacker's parry skill.

source.section: School Knacks > Counterattack

summary: School knack (Ring: Earth). This knack is used to detect the Shadowlands Taint in humans. To use it, you must spend a full minute concentrating on someone, who cannot leave your sight during this time.

source.section: School Knacks > Detect Taint

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). By engaging another character in conversation you may gain insight into that character's Honor. When you use this knack the GM tells you that character's honor + 0.5 * (1k1 - 5), where the 1k1 is rolled without rerolling 10s.

source.section: School Knacks > Discern Honor

summary: School knack (Ring: Fire). This is a type of attack roll, made in place of the attack skill, in which the TN to hit your target is raised by 20. If successful, roll extra damage dice as if the TN hadn't been raised, and inflict a serious wound in addition to the normal damage roll.

source.section: School Knacks > Double Attack

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). At the beginning of each combat round, you may breathe spiritual fire which extends around you 10 feet in every direction. These flames do not harm physical objects, except that they deal (2X)k1 damage to any characters you choose to be harmed, where X is your rank in this knack.

source.section: School Knacks > Dragon Tattoo

summary: School knack (Ring: Fire). This is a type of attack roll, made in place of the attack skill, that does no damage, but if successful it yields a temporary void point. Your highest action is then moved to the current phase.

source.section: School Knacks > Feint

summary: School knack (Ring: Fire). This is a type of attack roll even when not being used to attack; its full rules are explained with the other combat rules.

source.section: School Knacks > Iaijutsu

summary: School knack (Ring: Void). Spend a void and roll this knack to swap the highest and second highest Ring ranks of the target character for the remainder of one conversation or fight. In the case of a tie for the second-highest Ring, the target chooses which Ring is switched with the highest one.

source.section: School Knacks > Kharmic Spin

summary: School knack (Ring: Fire). This is a type of attack roll, made in place of the attack skill, that grants an extra die of damage if you hit. Everyone fighting you gets a free raise on their next attack against you this round.

source.section: School Knacks > Lunge

summary: School knack (Ring: Air). You have such command over factual arguments that you can trip others up. Once per conversation you may target a character, roll this knack, and divide the result by 5, rounding down.

source.section: School Knacks > Oppose Knowledge

summary: School knack (Ring: Water). You have such command over social situations that you can trip others up. Once per conversation you may target a character, roll this knack, and divide the result by 5, rounding down.

source.section: School Knacks > Oppose Social

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). When rolling a basic skill, you may increase the skill's rank by one, to a maximum of five. This may be done multiple times on the same roll, but only a number of times per adventure equal to twice your rank in this knack.

source.section: School Knacks > Otherworldliness

summary: School knack (Ring: Water or Air). Once per conversation, you may use your practiced aura of knowledgeable confidence to roll this knack instead of any basic skill when making an uncontested roll. This knack may be rolled with either Water or Air, whichever is higher at the time it is rolled.

source.section: School Knacks > Pontificate

summary: School knack (Ring: Water). Once per conversation, you may use your practiced presence of authority to roll this knack instead of any skill when making a contested roll initiated by another character.

source.section: School Knacks > Presence

summary: School knack (Ring: varies). To cast a spell, you spend actions equal to its mastery level minus 2. You then roll this knack with the Ring of that spell's element against a TN of its mastery level times 5.

source.section: School Knacks > Spellcasting

summary: School knack (Ring: N/A). Each adventure, you may spend a number of extra void points equal to the rank of this knack.

source.section: School Knacks > Worldliness

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Air). The main use of acting is helping your basic skills; you receive one free raise on all sincerity, intimidation, and sneaking rolls which are used to blend into crowds for every point of acting your character has. However, less scrupulous characters can also use it to pretend to be from another social class.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Acting

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). Make an open bragging roll whenever you want to convince someone that you're very talented or well qualified in some area. This can represent bragging about either your skill in general or one of your specific accomplishments.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Bragging

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Water). Most samurai have only the vaguest notion of how money even works; their needs are provided for by their daimyo. This skill grants an understanding of how money, taxes, and businesses all function and interact.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Commerce

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). Being cultured is very important to the samurai caste. This ranges from knowing which arts and fashions are in style to being well versed in literature and drama.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Culture

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). Protocol is extremely important in Rokugan, particularly for encounters which are formal and/or with people you've just met. In these situations, make an open etiquette roll to act suitably genteel.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Etiquette

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). When dealing with any House, it pays to know the local politics, especially alliances and feuds between its officials. GMs should take the question being asked and assign a base TN according to the chart below, with three potential modifications to the TN: - up to +/- 20 based on how familiar the PCs are with the...

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Heraldry

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Water). With over 1,000 years of history, you'll rarely encounter situations in Rokugan which haven't happened before. Make an open roll with this skill to cite a historical example in an unopposed argument, and roll contested when someone argues against you.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > History

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Air). Roll this contested against the sincerity of an NPC when you wish to detect whether they're lying. If you are speaking to them casually rather than grilling them, they get 2 free raises.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Interrogation

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). Make an open intimidation roll when you wish to either make overt threats or be implicitly menacing. This can represent either direct threat of physical violence or more subtle consequences.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Intimidation

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). Finding criminals often requires many skills, from looking for clues to identifying forgeries to breaking codes to following the tracks of a fleeing suspect. Rolls you make with this skill have TNs, but the GM will not reveal them; this is an exception to the rule that TNs are known to players.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Investigation

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). Rokugani law gives enormous discretion to magistrates, so what you're forbidden or permitted to do often depends on whether you can convince NPCs that your actions are legitimate. Conversely, you may try to compel NPCs to take some action by claiming that it's legally mandated.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Law

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Air). Roll this skill contested against another character's tact when you wish to demand an explanation for something that character said. This can involve twisting their words to seem insulting, or even making it look like they're saying something they didn't intend to.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Manipulation

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). Samurai live and die by what they believe to be right, and their sense of morality is based on a thousand years of writings on ethical living. Use this to argue that your position is the most righteous by citing tenets of bushido, sayings of Shinsei, etc.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Precepts

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). The most common use of this skill is to lie; in this case it is rolled contested against interrogation. However, you also make an open roll when making a statement of commitment or convincing argument which depends on an NPC believing that you're sincere.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Sincerity

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). Your character might occasionally wish to go somewhere without being remembered or perhaps without being seen at all. This skill is always rolled contested against the investigation of potential observers, whether your character is trying to remain completely hidden or is simply having minor interactions with NPCs...

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Sneaking

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Water). This skill grants an understanding of tactics as well as how to actually command forces of troops, police, etc. It also gives a working knowledge of bandits, mercenaries, and creatures from the Shadowlands.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Strategy

summary: Skill (basic, Ring: Air). Sometimes you have to speak unpleasant truths and/or say things which might not be well received. Make an open tact roll before saying something which you know might offend someone.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Tact

summary: Skill (advanced, Ring: Water). Bandits, smugglers, bloodspeakers, opium dens, gambling houses, and even ninja are rife throughout Rokugan. This skill grants understanding of how these groups function and how they interact with one another.

source.section: Skills > Detailed Skill Rules > Underworld

source.section: Advantages

summary: Advantage (3 XP). You heal two serious wounds instead of one the first night after being wounded.

source.section: Advantages

source.section: Advantages

summary: Advantage (8 XP). You get a free raise on wound checks.

source.section: Advantages

summary: Advantage (2 XP). You get a free raise on strategy and history rolls.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (6 XP). You have done something in the past which is considered disgraceful, and one of the PCs and a small number of NPCs (chosen by the GM) know about it. Characters who know your secret treat you as if your Rank and Recognition were 6.0 lower.

source.section: Disadvantages

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (5 XP). You have some ultimate goal which you want to achieve so badly that you'll disregard the adventure goal in order to pursue it.

source.section: Disadvantages

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (2 XP). Bragging rolls about your accomplishments are unaffected by this disadvantage, as are the Rank and Recognition bonuses you receive for them. However, while you may speak well of your accomplishments, you are self-deprecating about your skills and talents.

source.section: Disadvantages

source.section: Disadvantages

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (2 XP). You want to know everything that's going on and investigate every interesting event around you. Any intriguing goings-on simply have to be looked into, no matter how sensitive the issue.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (12 XP). It takes one fewer serious wound to kill you. You may not take the Great Destiny advantage.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (4 XP). Divide your Rank in half for the purpose of calculating your stipend. You may not take the Wealthy advantage, and you may not take this in a campaign in which you do not receive a stipend.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (2 XP). You are a shameless self-promoter who will never be self-deprecating or play down accomplishments. You will never directly apologize or admit a mistake even when actually at fault.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (3 XP). You do not heal the first night after being wounded, but heal normally after that.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (8 XP). You are easily insulted and must react immediately against perceived slights, particularly when they are related to matters of honor.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (5 XP). You don't think before you speak, and sometimes you cross lines you didn't see. People have 4 free raises when using Manipulation on you, and 2 free raises when rolling Manipulation against anyone on your side of an argument.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (12 XP). You are always considered to have rolled a 5 on sincerity rolls when lying or otherwise concealing information.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (4 XP). You have a slightly unusual way of approaching some aspect of bushido which can sometimes make you seem less honorable than you are at first. Whenever someone uses the discern Honor knack on you, instead of adding 0.5 * (1k1 - 5) to your honor, the GM subtracts the absolute value of that number.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (4 XP). You are less diligent about cleanliness and grooming than is considered proper. As a result, some characters will view you as uncivilized or undisciplined, and you get a -10 penalty to all culture rolls.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (8 XP). Once per adventure, the GM may apply a -5 penalty to any non-initiative roll.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (2 XP). You clearly care a great deal about your appearance, which to some is unseemly and unmanly.

source.section: Disadvantages

summary: Disadvantage (4 XP). You are very reserved and only speak when you feel you have something to say, and even then you express it as succinctly as possible without giving much regard to social niceties. As a result, your etiquette and open sincerity rolls are never considered to be higher than 15.

summary: The five main attributes: Air (reaction, social interaction, parry), Fire (action, speed, attacks), Earth (stamina, how wounded you can become), Water (focus, perception, memory, wound checks) and Void (inner balance, number of actions per round). Rings start at 2 (your School Ring at 3), maximum 5 (School Ring 6).

source.section: Character Creation > The Five Rings

summary: The Ring your school focuses on; it starts at 3 and can reach 6.

source.section: Character Creation > Schools

summary: L7R uses ten-sided dice. A roll is written XkY: roll X dice (skill + Ring) and keep the Y highest (the Ring), adding them. A 10 is rerolled and added. No roll uses more than 10 dice; extra rolled dice become kept dice, and each die beyond 10k10 adds +1.

source.section: Character Creation > Rolling Dice

summary: Target number: what a roll must meet or exceed to succeed. The GM normally says the TN before you roll so you can decide whether to spend void points.

source.section: Skills > Types of Rolls

summary: An open roll has a range of results (higher is better) rather than pass/fail. A contested roll pits two characters' rolls against each other; you get a free raise per point your skill exceeds the opponent's. Interrogation vs sincerity, manipulation vs tact and investigation vs sneaking always contest each other, the first winning ties.

source.section: Skills > Types of Rolls

summary: A +5 bonus to a roll's total, granted by the GM for circumstances or automatically by advantages and school abilities.

source.section: Skills > Types of Rolls

summary: Your maximum equals your lowest Ring. Before a roll you may spend void points (no more than your lowest Ring on one roll) to roll and keep one extra die each. You regain one after 8 hours of sleep.

source.section: Character Creation > Void Points

summary: Chosen at character creation: a School Ring, a special ability, three school knacks and five techniques (one per Dan, First to Fifth). Your Dan equals your lowest school knack.

source.section: Character Creation > Schools

summary: A character's level of mastery in their school, equal to their lowest school knack (First to Fifth); each Dan grants a technique.

source.section: Character Creation > Schools

summary: A school-specific ability rolled or used like a skill, starting at 1 and raised like an advanced skill; you can never use a knack your school lacks. Examples: feint, iaijutsu, double attack, counterattack, lunge, athletics, discern honor, worldliness.

source.section: Character Creation > Schools

summary: Basic social skills: bragging, etiquette, intimidation, sincerity, sneaking, tact; advanced: acting, interrogation, manipulation. Basic knowledge skills: culture, heraldry, investigation, law, precepts, strategy; advanced: commerce, history, underworld. Plus attack and parry. Rolling a skill at 0 means no rerolled 10s (and -10 if advanced).

source.section: Skills > Skill List

summary: Each 10-phase combat round you roll Void+1 dice (no rerolls, no void) and keep all but the highest: these action dice say in which phases you act. An unspent action becomes a held action usable later in the round; spending any two action dice makes an interrupt action to parry.

source.section: Combat > Initiative

summary: Attack (Fire) has a TN of 5 + 5 x the defender's parry skill; a hit can then be parried (Air) with the attack roll as the TN. Parrying for an ally raises that TN by 5 x the attacker's attack skill. Declaring a parry before the attack is rolled gives a free raise.

source.section: Combat > Attacking and Parrying

summary: Damage adds to your light wound total; you then roll (Water+1)k(Water) as a wound check against it. Failing gives 1 serious wound (+1 per 10 failed by) and clears light wounds; succeeding lets you keep them or take 1 serious wound to clear them. Serious wounds equal to your Earth leave you impaired (no rerolled 10s on skills); twice your Earth is mortally wounded. One serious wound heals every other night.

source.section: Combat > Damage

summary: Weapon base damage is katana 4k2, spear or wakizashi 3k2, knife 2k2, unarmed 0k2, plus your Fire in rolled dice, plus a die for every 5 the attack beat its TN (reduced by the defender's parry if they tried and failed to parry). No void points on damage.

source.section: Combat > Damage

summary: Duelists show their stance (an iaijutsu/Air open roll to gauge the other's Fire and TN), make a contested iaijutsu roll, then take turns to focus (+5 to their own TN to be hit) or strike (both attack at once, an extra damage die per 1 over the TN, no void, no rerolled 10s). Once someone is hit the duel becomes ordinary combat.

source.section: Combat > Iaijutsu Duels

summary: A character surrounded by two or more gives every attacker +5 + 5 per surrounder to attack rolls; slipping between two opponents gives each a free provoked attack.

source.section: Combat > Movement and Positioning

summary: Bow attacks use the attack skill; holding the action adds +1 per phase held; every hit deals an automatic serious wound (two with double attack) plus 10k2 to 10k8 damage; distance raises the TN to be hit.

source.section: Combat > Archery Rules

summary: Honor is the strength of your convictions (low-honor characters are exactly as good as their incentives); Recognition is fame; Rank is official position, which also sets your stipend (Rank squared in koku per year).

source.section: Character Creation > Honor, Recognition, and Rank

summary: Experience points, spent to raise Rings, skills, knacks and Honor and to buy advantages; disadvantages give XP. A new samurai averages about 150 XP.

source.section: Character Creation > The Five Rings

summary: Ability sets for non-samurai characters in place of a school: wave man (combat), worker and merchant (with money bonuses), priest rituals, and ninja.

source.section: Professions

summary: A Lion school; School Ring Water; knacks double attack, feint, iaijutsu. Special ability: You get four temporary void points after a successful feint and one void point after an unsuccessful feint.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Akodo Bushi

summary: A Scorpion school; School Ring Fire; knacks double attack, feint, iaijutsu. Special ability: When spending void points on all types of attack rolls, add 1k1 to the damage rolls of those attacks per void point spent.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Bayushi Bushi

summary: A Crane school; School Ring Water; knacks counterattack, double attack, iaijutsu. Special ability: You may counterattack as an interrupt action by spending only one action die, but if you do so then your target gets a free raise on their wound check if you hit. You may counterattack for other characters at no penalty.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Daidoji Yojimbo

summary: A Crab school; School Ring Water; knacks counterattack, double attack, iaijutsu. Special ability: You may counterattack as an interrupt action by spending only one action die, but if you do so then the attacker gets a free raise on their attack roll.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Hida Bushi

summary: A Crab school; School Ring Air; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: The two allies fighting on your left and right have their TN to be hit raised by 5.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Hiruma Scout

summary: A Phoenix school; School Ring Water; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: You add your Water instead of Fire to your rolled damage dice.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Isawa Duelist

summary: A Crane school; School Ring Fire; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: Your 10s on initiative rolls are considered to be in a special Phase 0. You may use interrupt actions to attack using iaijutsu, and any Phase 0 attacks use iaijutsu.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Kakita Duelist

summary: A Dragon school; School Ring Water; knacks discern Honor, iaijutsu, presence. Special ability: You use Water for interrogation rolls, and you add twice your Water to attack rolls.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Kitsuki Magistrate

summary: A Crab school; School Ring Earth; knacks detect Taint, iaijutsu, presence. Special ability: You may never become Tainted. Roll an extra (X+1)k(X+1) on wound checks, where X is the Shadowlands Taint of the attacker (rounded down to the nearest whole number).

source.section: Samurai Schools > Kuni Witch Hunter

summary: A Lion school; School Ring Fire; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: You always roll 10 dice when rolling initiative, keeping the usual number as action dice.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Matsu Bushi

summary: A Dragon school; School Ring Void; knacks counterattack, double attack, iaijutsu. Special ability: Your successful or unsuccessful parries give you a temporary void point.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Mirumoto Bushi

summary: A Unicorn school; School Ring Fire; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: After an attack against you is completely resolved, you may make a lunge attack at your attacker as an interrupt action at the cost of one action die.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Otaku Bushi

summary: A Phoenix school; School Ring Air; knacks counterattack, double attack, iaijutsu. Special ability: You may parry as an interrupt action by spending your lowest action die, and you may parry attacks directed at other characters with no penalty.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Shiba Bushi

summary: A Unicorn school; School Ring Air; knacks double attack, iaijutsu, lunge. Special ability: Each action you take in combat has a bonus of 2X, where X is the number of phases for which the action die was held.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Shinjo Bushi

summary: A Scorpion school; School Ring Earth; knacks double attack, feint, iaijutsu. Special ability: Gain a temporary void point every time you take a serious wound.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Yogo Warden

summary: A school with no clan; School Ring Any non-Void; knacks conviction, otherworldliness, worldliness. Special ability: You roll and keep one extra die for damage rolls from unarmed attacks.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Brotherhood of Shinsei Monk

summary: A school with no clan; School Ring Air; knacks discern Honor, oppose social, worldliness. Special ability: Add your Air to attack and damage rolls.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Courtier

summary: A Crane school; School Ring Air or Water; knacks counterattack, oppose social, worldliness. Special ability: You may spend a void point to counterattack as an interrupt action at the cost of one action die; this void point still gives your counterattack +1k1. Your counterattack rolls receive a bonus equal to the attacker's roll

summary: A Unicorn school; School Ring Any non-Void; knacks double attack, feint, worldliness. Special ability: After a feint which met its TN, lower the TN of the target by 10 the next time they are attacked, even if the feint was parried.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Ide Diplomat

source.section: Samurai Schools > Merchant

summary: A school with no clan; School Ring Any non-Void; knacks conviction, otherworldliness, pontificate. Special ability: You have all 10 rituals listed under the Priest profession.

source.section: Samurai Schools > Priest

If you roll 1 die, it may only be spent on athletics actions; if you roll 3 dice, all of your action dice may only be spent on athletics actions

summary: A Imperial school; School Ring Any; knacks iaijutsu, oppose (combined oppose knowledge and oppose social which applies to all skills and all characters opposing you), declaration (combined presence and pontificate - you may use this as one of each per conversation). Special ability: Add your Rank to open, TN, and contested rolls.

source.section: Non-Player-Character Schools > Hantei

summary: A Fox school; School Ring Any non-Void; knacks absorb void, commune, iaijutsu. Special ability: Once per target per combat round or conversation, you may substitute your School Ring in place of the usual ring when making a roll involving that target.

source.section: Spells

summary: A PC-only resource for desperate moments: spend one to regain a void point, add a free raise to a roll, reroll a roll, or ignore impairment to reroll 10s. Each costs XP (1, then 2, then 3...).

source.section: Player Character Points

summary: In "between places" rolls become dice pools counting successes (each die meeting the adjusted difficulty; a 10 always succeeds and rerolls).

source.section: Between Places

summary: Dream quests and spirit encounters use special rolls (Void plus another Ring, two skills, counting only dice that roll a 10), scenes along elemental paths, and can deal skill or connection damage.

source.section: Spirit Encounters

summary: Battle rules built on fighting posture, levels of engagement (disengaged, skirmishing, clashing, intense fighting), the tide of battle and individual or unit-level heroic opportunities.

source.section: Mass Combat

summary: Taint is measured in tenths; below 1.0 the body purges it (0.1 per 10 days, helped by a precepts roll and jade); at 1.0 it is permanent and costs many school abilities; 6.0 kills.
